items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer lists Les Hite as a band that came after Ernie Fields in poll rankings; the interviewee does not respond with any personal connection or interaction.

ctx.x: I really don't know if that was the last poll opinions, but anyway, for several years I was in the top ten.

Well look at the bands below you. After you comes Earl Hines, Andy Kirk, Nobel Cecil, Les Hite, Ella Fitzgerald, John Kirby, Cecil Burke, Tiny Bradshaw, Swinging Rays, Claude Hopkins, Fats Waller, Adie South, Al Cooper--that would be the Savoy Sultans-- Coban Hawkins and Lucky Millinder.
Those came after that I just named.

items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: He was a very fine guy and everything, and Les was a fine arranger too.

ctx.x: with the first band I went to New York with. MR. FIELDS: Sure enough. MR. LOVE: Snub Mosley, 1943; earlier in the year. I joined Basie later that year. Leslie just died a year or two ago in Oklahoma City. MR. FIELDS: Yes, he sure did. I was fortunate enough--I don't call the funeral fortunate--but I was glad I was around to go. MR. LOVE: What did he die from? MR. FIELDS: Cancer. MR. LOVE: Did you know Rudy Morrison? MR. FIELDS: Yeah, sure, Rudy played with me also. MR. LOVE: I know. We worked together too. MR.…
Yeah a number of years, but it hasn't been too long for Leslie. He was a very fine guy and everything, and Les was a fine arranger too.
